problem: Object-goal navigation frameworks based on object-scene memory and temporal attention (e.g., OMT) leave termination control (when to issue Done) underexplored, causing premature or missed stops.
motivation: Correct stopping is critical for success in ObjectNav, and RGB features plus 2D semantics may not give reliable evidence of true proximity to the target. Explicit depth cues might provide additional evidence for the stop decision.
key_idea: Add a learnable depth-aware gate on top of an OMT-based RL (PPO) navigation policy that regulates the termination decision while leaving the RGB backbone unchanged.
insight: Per the abstract's ablation, under the tested gate design, RGB features and 2D semantic statistics alone are insufficient for reliable termination, while adding explicit depth cues yields more accurate stopping. Termination can thus be improved by a separate depth-conditioned module without retraining the navigation backbone. Only the abstract was available, so details are limited.
method: Object Memory Transformer (OMT) backbone: RGB-based object-scene memory and temporal attention navigation policy, kept unchanged.
Depth-aware gate: a learnable gate that uses explicit depth cues to regulate the termination (Done) decision.
PPO training: reinforcement learning, compared with a PPO no-gate baseline.
Ablation of gate inputs: RGB features and 2D semantic statistics alone versus including depth.

setting.backbone: OMT (Object Memory Transformer) with PPO plus a learnable depth-aware gate
setting.training_data: AI2-THOR episodes trained with RL (PPO); scale not given in abstract
setting.observation: RGB plus depth (depth used by the gate), 2D semantic statistics
setting.action_space: discrete low-level actions including a termination (Done) action

results: On AI2-THOR, the depth-aware gate improves both stopping accuracy and overall navigation performance over a PPO no-gate baseline. Ablations show that gates without depth are insufficient. No numbers are given in the abstract.
limitations: Evaluated only on AI2-THOR, with no real-robot evidence stated.
Conclusions are limited to the tested gate design, as the abstract itself notes.
